slides.heading: Market: Fed Day, Saylor Sits One Out
slides.body: Five red days into Monday, a dip under $80K, then a bounce into the Fed. Decision at 2pm Eastern. A hold at 3.75–4% was priced near certain; December hike expected.
bullets: ETFs: +$301M last week despite Thursday's $636M outflow, biggest since June. Mon +$110M, Tue +$176M, IBIT 86% of it. October still net negative
Strategy bought NO bitcoin Oct 19–25. Holdings stay 848,517. $205M into STRC buybacks instead, second week running. STRC holders voted 99.3% for daily dividends
Strive +6,182 BTC, now 43,000. Price undisclosed. SATA preferred pays 13%, daily
Bottom calls: Galaxy's Thorn says the bear ended in June under $58K. Bitwise's 2036 base case now $1.6M. Opinions, not data
Noise: oil over $100 on an Iran-strikes report, Bank of Canada hiked, dollar at a 2026 high. Midterms Tuesday

topics.title: Hardware Wallets in Hot Water
topics.description: Passport customers phished from Foundation's own domains; Keystone shreds 18,835 devices after its factory key leaks. Your coins are fine. Your address isn't

slides.heading: Hardware Wallets in Hot Water: Passport
slides.body: Sunday night, Passport owners got an email from Foundation's real domain: your funds are at risk, a supplier tampered with displays, follow this urgent recall. The link asked for your 12 words.
bullets: Real names, addresses and order dates in the email. Landed in inboxes, not spam. Over 23,000 attempts counted
How: a self-hosted app (Cal.com) on the backend was breached, likely exposing the support inbox. Cloudflare keys revoked, fake site down, attackers cut off within 10 minutes of the first reports
The real failure: orders looked redacted after 60 days, but database migrations left copies in old tables. Refunds and abandoned carts too, so people who never bought got the email
Devices and keys untouched. Zach Herbert: "I'm very sorry." Formal report promised, not out yet
Foundation's banner says it: any email claiming your Passport funds are at risk is a scam

slides.heading: Hardware Wallets in Hot Water: Keystone Shreds 18,835
slides.body: Same week, worse week. Keystone's website was breached Oct 20 through a third-party monitoring tool. The attacker left with customer records and the key that proves a Keystone is genuine.
bullets: That WebAuth key is burned in at the factory and can't be rotated. With it, a counterfeit passes Keystone's own check. So: 18,835 unsold devices destroyed, shipping paused, web sales become preorders
25,964 buyer records still held names and addresses, plus 12,873 abandoned checkouts. Keystone advertised 180-day deletion; the erasure jobs had been failing silently
Delivered before Oct 20: fine. After: contact support, because the online check can't tell real from fake anymore
2026 tally: Ledger implants ($102M, 324 wallets), Coldcard's entropy bug, Trezor's two leaks, Foundation, Keystone. None of this week's touched a seed. All touched an address
Lopp: a custodian relocates risk, doesn't remove it. Multisig across locations and vendors. Nur Khalil in Forbes: self-custody needs accountability, or people stay in ETFs

topics.title: Mining: Winter Is Coming
topics.description: Hashrate back over a zettahash, difficulty up again Thursday, miners restarting old rigs. Then the home angle: a water heater that mines, and a Bitaxe firmware patch you should install

slides.heading: Mining: Winter Is Coming (That's Good)
slides.body: The 12-month thesis: price is off the June low, the idle fleet is already back, the big public miners are turning sites into AI data centers, and winter makes heat worth money. The live state:
bullets: Hashrate 1,083 EH/s, 7% off the record. Back over 1 ZH/s on Oct 11, first time since June. January's low was 826. October is the best month since December
Difficulty 140.58T after +5.92% on Oct 16. Thursday: about +6.3% to ~149T, highest since last November. Live estimate, moves every block
Hashprice $36 per PH/day, down from $47 a year ago. June's $30 was the record low: over 27 J/TH lost money on power, 227 EH/s went dark. Most of it is back
The AI drain: Riot leased 191 MW at Rockdale to Anthropic, $9.1B over 20 years. Core Scientific 377 MW to AMD. CleanSpark, TeraWulf, Bitdeer converting. Sites leave; machines move to cheaper power
Break-even, my arithmetic, power only at $36: 15 J/TH clears at 8¢/kWh. 20 J/TH needs under 7.5¢. 30 J/TH needs 5¢ to break even. Thursday cuts everyone ~6%
slides.linkLabel: Tokenist: hashrate near record, hashprice down 23%

slides.heading: Mining: Heatbit Puts an ASIC in Your Water Heater
slides.body: Bitwater, announced Oct 22: a standard screw-in water-heater element with 20 Bitmain BM1370 chips where the resistance wire used to be. The tank water is the cooling. No fans, no noise.
bullets: Up to 34 TH/s at up to 600 W, from 12 J/TH. Fits the 1-inch port on any 30–80 gallon electric tank in the US and Canada. Replaces the lower element; the upper stays as backup
Install yourself: breaker off, drain, unscrew the old element, screw in Bitwater, connect the app. Heating works offline, mining needs internet. Your own pool and address
$899 Genesis batch, refundable, ships Q1 2027. Later batches up to $1,299. One-year warranty. Gas and heat-pump versions promised
The money: Heatbit won't quote a number. Decrypt's math at today's hashprice: about $1.25 a day, $455 a year. Two-year payback, before Thursday's bump
The pitch that matters: 600 W of heat is 600 W of heat. You were paying for that electricity anyway. The sats are a rebate on a bill you already had

slides.heading: Mining: Bitaxe, Proto Boards, and Lightning Payouts
slides.body: Three smaller pieces of the same story: patch your Bitaxe, buy a Proto board if you want hosted hashrate you own, and take your pool payouts over Lightning.
bullets: Bitaxe firmware 2.15.4 (Oct 21) has one change: Skot replaced the certificate store after the eMudhra CA compromise. Eight CA keys were recoverable from the certs; every browser blocked them. Same cleanup Keep did last week. Update over OTA
No Bitaxe block since July's 3.14 BTC. Two unattributed solo blocks this month. The Intel-chip Bonanza repo got pushes, still no spec

Sazmining sells Block's Proto immersion boards to individuals: ~200 TH at 15 J/TH, from $1,397 with 0% financing, hosted in the US, rewards to your wallet. "We only earn when we produce bitcoin for our clients"
Landfall (Vincenzo Palazzo): OCEAN payouts over Lightning from one recovery phrase. Makes the address, the BOLT12 offer and the BIP322 signature OCEAN wants. A showcase, not a product
The ladder: $150 Bitaxe, $899 water heater, $1,397 Proto board, Lightning payouts for all of them

links.label: Bitcoin Magazine: Sazmining sells Proto boards

topics.title: Core 32.1: The Real 32.0
topics.description: Core says 32.0 "was never fully announced or released." 32.1 is today's release, 29.x is dead, and easy-to-find bugs no longer get an embargo

slides.heading: Core 32.1: The Real 32.0
slides.body: Last week: Core 32.0 shipped 11 days late. Correction from bitcoincore.org: 32.0, "although tagged, was never fully announced or released." 32.1 went up today; 31.2 tagged the same minute.
bullets: Everything from last week still applies: 200 connections with half reserved for block-only peers, global relay backlog, Tor proof-of-work, the private-broadcast fix, PSBT v2 default, mempool fee estimator
New in the notes: walletnotify command injection. An RPC user allowed to create wallets could run shell commands via a crafted wallet name. Non-Windows, since 24.0
Probable reason for the do-over: the 32.0 GUI wrote PSBT v2 files older co-signers couldn't import, milestoned 32.1 on Oct 21. My inference; Core hasn't said
29.x and older: end of life. In two weeks, three medium-or-high bugs fixed in 30.0 get disclosed

New policy (Poinsot, merged Oct 22): a bug that's easy to find, "a simple prompt to a language model" being the yardstick, skips the embargo and ships on every branch at once. "The embargo period achieves little"

topics.title: Lightning Corner: Wavelength and Eclair
topics.description: Lightning Labs opens its Ark to everyone on mainnet, aimed at AI agents. Eclair patches two ways to steal from a forwarding node

slides.heading: Lightning Corner: Wavelength Goes Mainnet, Eclair Patches Theft
slides.body: Wavelength is Lightning Labs' Ark, open to everyone on mainnet since Oct 23. "Bitcoin on easy mode": no node, no channels, no liquidity, a few API calls. The audience is software, not people.
bullets: Agents pay per request with L402 and drive the wallet over MCP. Levin: give a service "only the right to receive payments, with no access to signing or recovery." Alpha, 300,000-sat cap, 0.25% plus routing, refresh every two weeks to keep your exit
Eclair 0.14.4 and 0.14.5, security releases: a payer could steal from a trampoline node by inflating expiry on retry; a taproot peer could lie about a splice input and claim an HTLC twice. Upgrade
Also: LND 0.21.5 and 0.20.6 RCs, LDK's one-hop BOLT12 fix, LND's experimental jamming reputation score, log-only
BOLT11: invoices must carry exactly one payment hash and one secret. That's the parser mismatch LNP2PBot got robbed with. BTCPay fixed duplicate payouts and an API-key escalation
Lichen, Adam Gibson's LN-GAP sequel: a single-issuer L2 where your exit is a proof the sequencer signed your withdrawal, disputed step by step with BitVMX. No committee this time

topics.title: Delving Grab-Bag
topics.description: The bitcoin-dev list finally readable, a payments post-mortem, another AI-written node, and a redaction option for node runners

slides.heading: Delving Grab-Bag: 15 Years of bitcoin-dev, Readable
slides.body: Four threads worth your time, starting with the one you'll actually use.
bullets: LearnBitcoin.com rebuilt the bitcoin-dev list: 24,699 messages, one page per thread, quotes folded, permalinks by Message-ID, indexes by BIP and author, refreshed daily

"The Long Road to Bitcoin Payments": a payments app used to take a team a year, now one prompt. A million Square merchants accept bitcoin, almost nobody pays with it. Stripe, Shopify, Coinbase picked stablecoins. The blocker is demand
rbitcoin 0.8.0: another Rust node, "entirely AI-written," relational archive instead of a UTXO set, BIP324 only. Last week's bitcoin-rs has company
Hash preimages in descriptors (João Dias): let Core's wallet hold a preimage like a key, so a hash-locked output spends without PSBT gymnastics
"Information hazards and safe redaction": a node option to drop data you consider hazardous and stay otherwise archival. The OP_RETURN war is becoming a config file

links.label: Delving: The Long Road to Bitcoin Payments

topics.title: Nostr This Week
topics.description: Bitchat makes crowded rooms fast and ships a panic wipe, Amethyst lands on Flathub with self-updates over Nostr, and slash commands become a NIP

slides.heading: Nostr This Week: Bitchat 1.8, Amethyst on Flathub
slides.body: No Nostr Compass this morning, so straight from the release pages.
bullets: Bitchat 1.8.0 (Oct 23): a 300-person geochat opens in 180 ms instead of 4 to 12 seconds. Messages matched by sender ID, not nickname, so a name-thief can't hijack your threads. Noise sessions rekey on age
Also in 1.8: drafts survive channel switches, one-tap join nearby, a verification seal in DMs, a panic wipe that asks first, 30 languages. BTC Sessions' no-app-store install guide is going around
Amethyst 1.20.0 (Oct 24): on Flathub, and the desktop updates itself from NIP-82 release events. Remote-signer relays now go over Tor. Emoji packs, draw-to-GIF, git repos from the app
NIPs: slash commands merged Oct 21, a list event Oct 27. What you type after a slash is now a spec, not a client quirk. ngit-cli 3.0.4 shipped
Carry-over: Zapstore 1.1.3 and Keep 1.3.2 from last week are the ones to install if you haven't

topics.title: FIPS Watch: Macs Join the Mesh
topics.description: No release this week, but 94 commits: a macOS Bluetooth backend, interfaces that can show up late, and the first outside contributors

slides.heading: FIPS Watch: Macs Join the Mesh Over Bluetooth
slides.body: Still v0.5.3, still pre-audit. But master had 94 commits in seven days and the unreleased changelog reads like a release. Three things, plus new names in the log.
bullets: CoreBluetooth backend: a Mac can peer over BLE with Android, Linux and other Macs. Mac to Android verified on hardware, the rest untested. macOS won't give Bluetooth to a root daemon, so a per-user agent lends the radio over a socket
Interfaces can appear late. An Ethernet transport binds when its interface shows up and rebinds when it returns. Closes the OpenWrt boot race where fips started before wifi made its mesh interfaces
The IPv6 adapter is its own module now, TCP links survive mismatched MTUs, and UDP can bind to one interface so two NICs are two routes

Outside the author for the first time: Origami74's multi-path switchover PR (one session, several transports) and a macOS BLE fix. Issues from rabble (Mac release?), franzaps of Zapstore, mmalmi of Iris
Still alpha, wire format not stable, no audit. Watch for 0.5.4

topics.title: Policy Corner: Russia Fences the Exit
topics.description: Russia plans to block withdrawals to self-custody, CLARITY stays stalled into the midterms, and Brazil's biggest bank registers to custody crypto

slides.heading: Policy Corner: Russia Fences the Exit
slides.body: Quiet week in Washington, loud week in Moscow.
bullets: Russia (via HRF): ban peer-to-peer trading, license nine institutions including VTB and Sberbank, and block withdrawals from them to your own wallet. Non-qualified investors, 98% of the market, get a test and a 300,000-ruble yearly cap
HRF's summary: bitcoin bought through an approved institution "must remain within the state-regulated financial system." Bitcoin stays legal. Leaving stays illegal

US: CLARITY stalled since the Sept 15 vote. Bessent Tuesday: the US "will win in digital assets," pitching a Plan B. TD Cowen: the midterms could freeze it two years. H.R. 8957 still parked at committee
Brazil: Itaú registered with the central bank to custody crypto under the new licensing rules
Carry-forwards: France's I-CF821 still needs a vehicle. MSCI's list lands Nov 11

topics.title: This Friday: PlebLab's AI Startup Rodeo
topics.description: One day, one stage, downtown Austin: machine-to-machine payments, with LDK, OpenAgents and PlebLab on the bill. $25, bring a builder free

slides.heading: This Friday: AI Startup Rodeo, Edition 02
slides.body: "Software is starting to pay software." Friday Oct 30, 9 to 5, Q Branch at The Texas Embassy, 200 E 6th St, Suite 300. Austin Tech Week. Talks and live demos, one room, one stage.
bullets: On the bill: Ben Carman (Spiral, LDK), Austen Allred (Gauntlet AI), Robert Willis (Tribe of Hackers), Christopher David (OpenAgents), HT of Sovereign Hybrid Compute, Soru Kumar (OrangeMetrics), Christopher Scott on threshold signing. Car Gonzalez and Roberto Fuentes organize
Theme fits this deck: Wavelength for agents, LDK Server's MCP bridge, L402 pay-per-request. This is the room where those get demoed
$25, and every ticket includes a free guest pass. Bring a builder. Breakfast, coffee and lunch included. Pay in bitcoin via Zaprite
Afterparty 5pm, Upstairs at Caroline, 621 Congress. Free drinks on the wristband
Call for papers still open, schedule "still filling." Edition 01 had 18 speakers including Core contributors; talks are on YouTube

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: LDK Server
topics.description: Ben Carman and Spiral's LDK Server: a full Lightning node as a daemon, now with an MCP bridge so an AI agent can run it as a tool

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: LDK Server, a Node Your Agent Can Drive
slides.body: LDK is the Lightning library inside dozens of wallets. LDK Server is that library turned into a full node you run as a daemon and talk to over RPC. The new piece: ldk-server-mcp, which exposes every unary RPC as an MCP tool.
bullets: What that means: point Claude, Goose or any MCP client at it and the agent can open channels, make invoices, pay and read balances with the same calls an app would. The node stays yours; the agent gets a tool list
The sober counterpart to Wavelength: Wavelength hides the node, LDK Server hands you one. Self-hosted, Rust, MIT/Apache, pushed Oct 26
Why Ben: LDK at Spiral, Mutiny Wallet before that, and on stage Friday at the Rodeo on exactly this
Try it: clone lightningdevkit/ldk-server, write a config.toml, cargo run the daemon, then cargo run -p ldk-server-mcp with the same config and add it to your MCP client
Caveat: it's a node with a hot wallet. Signet first, small on mainnet, and never give an agent more sats than you'd give an intern

links.label: See him Friday at the Rodeo

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Two wallet makers leaked customer addresses in one week. The recall email is the attack. Here's the reflex

slides.heading: Quick Tip: The Recall Email Is the Attack
slides.body: No hardware-wallet company will ever email you to type your words into a website, ship your device back, or "verify" your wallet. The email that says so is the attack.
bullets: Got one? Don't click. Type the vendor's address yourself and look for the banner. Foundation and Keystone both had one up within hours
Your 12 or 24 words go into exactly one place: the device that made them. A web page, a support chat, a form, a QR code: no
Assume your name and address are already out there. Two vendors proved "we delete after 60 days" wasn't true. Next purchase: a PO box, an alias email, pay in bitcoin
Bought from a reseller, or got a Keystone after Oct 20? Verify through the vendor's support before you fund it. Passing the website check is no longer proof
Big stack? Multisig across two vendors and two locations. One bad supply chain then costs you nothing
